new_statements.quote: Word stress in Liŋŋit̠iɣ is predictable: the first vowel which is preceded by a consonant is stressed. Accordingly, the first vowel is stressed in words beginning in a consonant or cluster -- kápan short, ŋgóðRo black -- but the second vowel in words which begin in a vowel -- ayóŋ I, alán sky, aðá crow. [p.179] ... At all events, Liŋŋit̠iɣ and Alŋit̠ (Alngith) are dialects of a single language, sharing 87 percent of basic vocabulary. [p.176]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the first vowel that is preceded by a consonant: on the first syllable of consonant-initial words, on the second syllable of vowel-initial words (the post-initial-dropping Northern Paman pattern; historically the etymological second syllable). Stated for Linngithigh; Hale treats Alngith as a co-dialect of the same language in the same source, so for Alngith this is a co-dialect inference, not a direct observation.
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned; stress described as fully predictable. Hale notes Linngithigh morphemes are predominantly monosyllabic and often begin in consonant clusters.
new_statements.domain_note: Word stress ('Word stress in Liŋŋit̠iɣ is predictable'), illustrated on isolated lexical items; pp.167-168 additionally give the diachronic Northern-Paman-wide shift of primary stress from the initial to the second syllable of Paman stems, which covers Alngith as a sampled variety.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted stress rule describes Linngithigh (Liŋŋit̠iɣ, Glottolog leni1238), not Alngith directly. Hale 1966 p.176 states in the same source that 'Liŋŋit̠iɣ and Alŋit̠ (Alngith) are dialects of a single language, sharing 87 percent of basic vocabulary' (Glottolog groups them as Linngithigh-Alngith, leni1237); Sutton & Hale 2021:117 repeat 'distinct but close dialects of a single language', and Wikipedia (citing Hale 1976a:14) reports identical sound inventories, Alngith differing by metathesis. Hale's own Alngith data are 3 leaves (AIATSIS MS 882 (12)). No Alngith-specific stress sentence was found in any opened source; the Alngith entry, if catalogued, should be flagged as a co-dialect inference from Linngithigh with the Northern-Paman-wide stress shift (Hale 1966:167-168) as the only group-level statement that names Alngith's group.

new_statements.relation_note: The group-level rule ('the first vowel that follows a consonant is stressed') is the same placement as the existing Hale 1966 Linngithigh statement (first vowel preceded by a consonant). Not a full read: the item is lending-only, the full text download could not be reached by automated download, so only 5-snippet-per-query volume-level hits were obtained, without page numbers and without proof that the rule sentence sits in the Alngith section (c. p.14 per Wikipedia). Confidence low.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Group-level Northern Paman rule as it appears in the volume's snippets: stress falls on the first vowel that follows a consonant (initial syllable in consonant-initial words, second syllable in vowel-initial words), described as the synchronic outcome of a historical shift of stress from the first to the second syllable. The snippets do not show the sentence attached to Alngith specifically; Alngith appears only in the source-abbreviation list and in the group heading '[Mpalitjanh, Alngith, Awngthim, Ntra'ngith and Mbiywom]'.
new_statements.exceptions: a snippet begins 'With certain' after the rule, so the volume states exceptions, but their content is cut off
new_statements.identity_note: The only full stress statement held by the project (Hale 1966 p.179) is for Linngithigh (leni1238), which Hale calls a co-dialect of a single language with Alngith (87 percent shared basic vocabulary, p.176). Hale 1976a treats Alngith inside the Northern Paman group [Mpalitjanh, Alngith, Awngthim, Ntra'ngith, Mbiywom] and, per Wikipedia citing p.14, says Alngith and Linngithigh share the same sound inventory. No Alngith-specific stress sentence has been seen in any opened text.

sources.note: p.179 (Linngithig sketch): 'Word stress in Liŋŋit̠iɣ is predictable: the first vowel which is preceded by a consonant is stressed' (kápan, ŋgóðRo vs ayóŋ, alán, aðá). p.176: 'Liŋŋit̠iɣ and Alŋit̠ (Alngith) are dialects of a single language, sharing 87 percent of basic vocabulary.' pp.167-168: Northern-Paman-wide 'shift of primary stress (a strictly phonetic feature) from the initial to the second syllable (*CV2) in Paman stems' (Alngith is in the 13-variety sample, p.163). No Alngith-specific synchronic stress sentence; Alngith forms appear only in the lexicostatistic table (p.175 'Alnit 59').
